q: A penniless migrant arrested for petty theft cannot engage counsel. He asks for legal help before the remand hearing at night.
options: Tell him free aid is only at trial, not at remand
Provide free legal aid at state cost and note request in remand diary
Ask complainant to pay lawyer fee as charity
Delay production till he arranges own lawyer
expl: State must provide free legal aid to indigent accused from first production.
why: Directive for free legal aid guides fair procedure and access to justice. On remand duty the SI must connect accused to legal services immediately.
trapnote: Trap: treats aid as trial-stage charity, not custody safeguard.

q: On outpost inspection you find farm labourers paid far below notified wages with children working in fields. The contractor says directives are not court-enforceable.
options: Ignore as directives cannot be enforced by police
Enforce minimum wage and child-labour laws, using directives to interpret duty
Fix wages yourself by panchayat order
Detain labourers to stop work
expl: Directives guide enforcement of enacted labour laws.
why: Directives for living wage and child welfare shape valid laws that police must enforce. On inspection the SI must apply the statutes, not cite non-justiciability to avoid action.
trapnote: Trap: non-justiciable means no police action.

q: A festival committee uses high-volume DJ till 2 am near a hospital, claiming celebration is a fundamental right and no one can stop.
options: Allow whole night as festival overrides all other concerns
Enforce noise limits and time restrictions to protect health and environment
Seize all equipment permanently without orders
Collect fine informally and permit violation
expl: Duty to protect environment and public health supports noise regulation.
why: Protection of environment and compassion for living creatures inform reasonable restrictions on celebration. On night patrol the SI must implement court and pollution norms, not ban festival outright.
trapnote: Trap: right to celebrate pitched as absolute.

q: During an agitation students damage buses and burn a police kiosk, saying protest duty excuses damage to public property.
options: Treat damage as part of protest and release them with warning
Register damage to public property case and remind duty to safeguard property
Recover loss by seizing any villager property at random
Refuse FIR as agitation is political matter
expl: Duty to safeguard public property condemns vandalism.
why: Fundamental duty to protect public property reinforces criminal law against mischief. On riot duty the SI must separate peaceful protesters from vandals and act on evidence.
trapnote: Trap: protest right excuse for vandalism.

q: A khap elders council orders boycott of a young couple for inter-caste marriage and asks you to enforce it for village peace.
options: Enforce boycott to preserve harmony and prevent clash
Protect couple, act against intimidation and uphold dignity and liberty
Send couple out of village for their safety permanently
Register case against couple for disobeying elders
expl: Directives for dignity and reform plus duty to renounce harmful customs bar khap diktats.
why: Goals of fraternity, dignity and reforming customs guide police to defend choice marriage. On village visit the SI must provide protection and bind over harassers.
trapnote: Trap: village peace plea to enforce illegal boycott.
